A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GDAGS and retain the same core research problem and method. Complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original rendering experiments across 13 scenes, split/clone ablations, parameter sensitivity tests and five-seed results in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark results, ablations, framework-transfer experiments, dropout studies and sparse-view tests in Section 4 and Appendices D–E.

M1.justification: The core GCR formula, power-law weighting, splitting rule and inverse weighting for cloning remain unchanged. Appendix D.4 introduces auxiliary random and opacity-weighted Gaussian-dropout variants that alter training, constituting a limited procedural extension.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate novel view synthesis on the same nine Mip-NeRF360 scenes and two scenes each from Tanks&Temples and Deep Blending. The added experiments reuse this coverage; the 50%-training-view test changes sample availability within the retained task.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Taming 3DGS and mini-splatting and removes the AbsGS-0008 comparison; the remaining AbsGS row matches the former AbsGS-0004 row. V2 also introduces comparisons involving MCMC-3DGS and Compact-3DGS in Table 3 and mini-splatting pruning variants in Table 6.

E3.justification: The original training schedule and default hyperparameters remain, but v2 substantially extends the evaluation design with 50%-view training, dropout-rate and opacity-weighted controls, a beta sweep, framework-integration experiments and dataset-level training-time/FPS evaluation. These are added protocols, not evidence that the retained benchmark training settings changed.

E4.justification: V2 adds framework-transfer tests, beta sensitivity, an exponential-weight alternative, dropout tests of the Deep Blending overfitting hypothesis and sparse-view robustness analysis. It also expands the existing linear-weight comparison from v1 Table 12 into the broader GDAGS-L evaluation in Table 2; the original split/clone and p-sensitivity analyses remain.

E5.justification: V1 Table 11 reports separate results for seeds 1–5 across all three datasets. V2 removes this entire repeated-run evidence without replacement uncertainty estimates; its generic reproducibility statement about documented seeds does not retain the reported variability.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes GDAGS's Mip-NeRF360 SSIM/PSNR/LPIPS from 0.821/27.55/0.199 to 0.839/28.02/0.145, retaining 515 MB. Tanks&Temples results and Pixel-GS's Mip-NeRF360 scores also change, while GDAGS's Deep Blending row remains unchanged. Numerous new results are added, including transfer experiments showing lower LPIPS alongside lower PSNR. The PDFs do not explain the source of the revised headline scores.

T1.justification: V1's von Mises-Fisher/Bessel and KL-variational derivation in Equations 6–11 is removed, with v2 motivating the retained weighting rule through design arguments. Appendix D.3 adds a mathematical comparison of power and exponential functions, substantially changing the theoretical support rather than merely its notation.

C1.justification: The central GCR and adaptive-weighting contributions remain. V2 removes the blanket 50% Gaussian/memory-reduction claim from the abstract and contribution list, and narrows the conclusion from avoiding heuristic threshold tuning to avoiding additional heuristic densification thresholds.

C2.justification: V2 introduces an overfitting explanation for Deep Blending behavior, interprets transfer and sparse-view tests as evidence of broader applicability, and argues that reduced Gaussian counts compensate for GCR computation overhead. It also expands parameter-selection guidance. The earlier limitations concerning fixed hyperparameters and extreme sparsity are retained.

D1.justification: Code-access instructions change from a GitHub link to an anonymous repository, with new statements about pretrained models, environment.yml, configurations and replication scripts. Appendix D.6 clarifies parameter selection and fixed settings across scenes. Conversely, v1's explicit Pixel-GS image-resolution qualification disappears.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands the relevant 3DGS literature, including Taming 3DGS, mini-splatting, MCMC-3DGS, Compact-3DGS, ReAct-GS and PSRGS. New discussion contrasts ReAct-GS/PSRGS complexity with GDAGS and connects the Deep Blending overfitting interpretation to ControlGS.

P1.justification: The weighting rationale and analysis narrative are substantially rewritten, Preliminary and Motivation exchange order, and the appendices are reorganized into dedicated algorithm, weighting, analysis, results and limitations sections. Ethics, reproducibility and LLM-usage statements are added, alongside author/header edits.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redesigned as a schematic-plus-results display, Figure 3 is condensed, and the weighting-response display gains beta curves. New transfer, sensitivity, function-comparison, dropout and efficiency displays substantially expand the presentation. Earlier appendix Figures 9–11 are retained as Figures 12–14, rather than newly added evidence.

improvement.justification: V2 adds valuable contemporary comparisons and targeted transfer, robustness and overfitting tests. However, it removes the five-seed results and introduces reliability problems: Tanks&Temples SSIM is 0.854 in Table 1 but 0.852 in Table 2, and Appendix D.3 contains incorrect derivative and endpoint-sign statements. Together with unexplained headline-score revisions, these losses make the net quality direction uncertain despite the broader empirical analysis.
